answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce stake before voting on reputation or earning pooled rewards. Influence is capped per stake, so splitting one deposit among a hundred accounts adds no weight. If a challenge proves fraud, the stake is slashed. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many independent deposits and risk losing them; minting names is not enough. A comet of accounts cannot evade the cap, even if they share a kernel and trade copper.
